items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'Misty' in the context of hand signals for band leaders; the interviewee confirms knowledge of the practice ('Oh yeah. The hand signals, sure.') but does not indicate a personal relationship with a person named Misty.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah I mean I made a living playing club dates for seven years when I first got married, and now they don’t have the same — there’s no market. It’s mostly DJs I think doing that kind of work. There are some bands working at that but I don’t know, I’ve been away from that for so long. But it was — and I must say that doing that kind of work you really learn a lot you know, you learn how to fake through tunes and, you know, they used to have bands that faked everything, you know pretty big sized, like a sax…
Oh yeah I’ve heard about that, like the band leader would say “Misty” and hold up three fingers or whatever, and then as “Misty” would come to an end they’d call another tune, two flats.
Oh yeah. The hand signals, sure. And the guys would fake harmonies and you know there was a certain pool of musicians who were excellent at that.
